tasks.title: Run the manual tenant validation workflow against a non-production Microsoft 365 tenant
evidence: `.github/workflows/release-tenant-validation.yml` requires `EXCHANGEADMIN_*` GitHub secrets and invokes `build/run-tenant-validation.ps1` to produce `artifacts/tenant-validation/tenant-validation-report.json`.
`docs/releases/verification.md` documents tenant validation as a separate manual release check that is not locally reproducible without a real tenant and certificate material.
tasks.impact: Release readiness for the certificate-backed Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph validation path remains unconfirmed until the manual workflow runs successfully against a non-production tenant.
tasks.recommended_action: Run `.github/workflows/release-tenant-validation.yml` or `build/run-tenant-validation.ps1` with the required certificate-backed app identity and retain the generated tenant validation report as release evidence.
tasks.blocker: Requires a real non-production tenant plus the certificate and GitHub secrets referenced by the workflow, which are not present in the repository or local context.
acceptance_criteria: The tenant validation workflow completes successfully and uploads `artifacts/tenant-validation/tenant-validation-report.json`.
The report records zero failed probes for the enabled Exchange Online and Microsoft Graph checks.

tasks.title: Run the unified setup EXE on a real 32-bit Windows host or VM
evidence: `scripts/pack.ps1` and `docs/releases/verification.md` describe a single setup EXE that must select the `artifacts/publish/win-x86` payload on 32-bit Windows.
`build/run-smoke-tests.ps1` validates reinstall and uninstall behavior locally, but the current repository context only provides a 64-bit Windows host.
tasks.impact: The installer path that selects and validates the x86 payload is still unverified on a real 32-bit Windows environment, so release evidence for that architecture is incomplete.
tasks.recommended_action: Run `artifacts/packages/OnlyExo365.Setup.exe` on a 32-bit Windows host or VM and confirm x86 payload selection, single uninstall entry preservation on reinstall, and clean uninstall behavior.
tasks.blocker: The current local verification context is a 64-bit Windows host only; no 32-bit Windows machine or VM is available in the repository context.
acceptance_criteria: The setup EXE installs the x86 payload on 32-bit Windows.
Reinstall keeps one Programs and Features entry for the product.
Uninstall removes the payload and uninstall registry entry cleanly on the 32-bit host.

tasks.title: Validate upgrade behavior from an ExchangeAdmin-branded install to the OnlyExo365-branded installer on a real Windows host
evidence: `installer/ExchangeAdmin.iss` and `docs/releases/verification.md` document a preserved installer AppId and reuse of the previous ExchangeAdmin install root during upgrade.

`src/ExchangeAdmin.Presentation/Services/ExchangeConfigurationLoader.cs`, `src/ExchangeAdmin.Contracts/Diagnostics/PersistentLogWriter.cs`, and `src/ExchangeAdmin.Contracts/Security/ProtectedSecretStore.cs` retain compatibility logic for legacy ExchangeAdmin configuration, log, and secret paths.
tasks.impact: The in-place upgrade path from an ExchangeAdmin-branded installation to the current OnlyExo365 installer is repository-supported but still unverified on a real machine, so upgrade and uninstall continuity remain release gaps.
tasks.recommended_action: Install a pre-rename ExchangeAdmin build on a Windows host, upgrade it with `artifacts/packages/OnlyExo365.Setup.exe`, then verify install-root reuse, configuration fallback, single uninstall entry continuity, and uninstall cleanup.
tasks.blocker: The current repository context does not include a provisioned host with a previously installed ExchangeAdmin build to exercise a real in-place upgrade path.
acceptance_criteria: An ExchangeAdmin-branded installation upgrades in place with the OnlyExo365 setup EXE without creating duplicate uninstall entries.
The upgraded install remains launchable and retains the expected configuration/data paths or documented fallback behavior.
Uninstall after upgrade removes the registered product and the documented default data roots cleanly.
